GALCEN_RA_DEG.description:
ICRS right ascension of the Galactic center, degrees. NaN means absent.
Sgr A*: 17h45m40.0409s (Reid & Brunthaler 2004, ApJ 616, 872).

GALCEN_DEC_DEG.description:
ICRS declination of the Galactic center, degrees. NaN means absent.
Sgr A*: -29d00m28.118s (Reid & Brunthaler 2004, ApJ 616, 872).

GALCEN_DISTANCE_PC.description:
Sun-to-Galactic-center distance R0, parsecs. NaN means absent.
Example: 8178 pc (GRAVITY Collaboration 2019, A&A 625, L10).

Z_SUN_PC.description:
Solar height above the Galactic midplane, parsecs, positive north.
NaN means absent; example: 20.8 pc (Bennett & Bovy 2019, MNRAS 482, 1417).

ROLL_DEG.description:
Roll angle in degrees in the Astropy Galactocentric convention.
NaN means absent, not zero. With GALACTIC axes, the five explicit scalar
parameters define a derived Galactocentric orientation: X points from
the Sun toward the center's projection in the midplane, Y follows
Galactic rotation, and Z completes a right-handed triad toward Galactic
north. This parameterized orientation is independent of ORIGIN; with
GALACTIC_CENTER the Sun lies at X=-sqrt(R0^2-Z_SUN_PC^2), Y=0, Z=Z_SUN_PC.
All five scalars must be finite for a spatial Galactocentric transform,
with R0 > 0 and abs(Z_SUN_PC) <= R0; none has an assumed default.

V_SUN_KMS.description:
Total solar velocity [v_X,v_Y,v_Z] in km/s in the resulting Galactocentric
axes, including circular motion (not just peculiar U,V,W). Exactly three
components when present; omit the vector when unknown, or use NaN for
an unknown component. A velocity transform requires all three finite.
Schonrich, Binney & Dehnen (2010), MNRAS 403, 1829, constrain peculiar
motion; Reid & Brunthaler (2020), ApJ 892, 39, constrain Sgr A* motion.
Publishers must state their adopted total velocity; no default is implied.

PPEPositionRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for Cartesian position
(and optionally velocity). Coefficients are stored per axis.

To evaluate position at time t within this record's validity window:
1. Compute normalized time: tau = (t - EPOCH_MID) / EPOCH_HALF_SPAN
where tau is in [-1, +1].
2. Evaluate the polynomial basis of degree (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1) using
the coefficients for each axis.

Velocity coefficients, if present, follow the same evaluation procedure.
If HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS is false, velocity can be obtained by
analytically differentiating the position polynomial.

EPOCH_MID.description:
Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).
Together with EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, defines the time interval:
[EPOCH_MID - EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, EPOCH_MID + EPOCH_HALF_SPAN]

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description:
Half-span of the validity window in seconds.
The full span is 2 * EPOCH_HALF_SPAN seconds centered on EPOCH_MID.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Number of polynomial coefficients per axis.
The polynomial degree is (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1).
Typical values: 8-32 for high-fidelity ephemeris fits.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POS_COEFF_X.description:

Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS. Ordered c0, c1, ..., c_{N-1}.

POS_COEFF_Y.description:

POS_COEFF_Z.description:

PPEOrbitalElementRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for classical orbital elements.

The six classical elements are:
1. SMA or R_PERIAPSIS (size/shape) — see SIZE_SHAPE_TYPE
2. Eccentricity (dimensionless)
3. Inclination (degrees)
4. Right Ascension of Ascending Node / RAAN (degrees)
5. Argument of Periapsis (degrees)
6. Anomaly (degrees) — see ANOMALY_TYPE

Evaluation follows the same normalized-time procedure as PPEPositionRecord.

1e-4 mm/s. Same base**n rule.

COMMENT.description: COMMENT lines of this covariance matrix (CCSDS 502.0-B-3), joined by a line feed.

COV_REFERENCE_FRAME.description:
COV_REF_FRAME of this matrix (CCSDS 502.0-B-3): the frame the matrix
is expressed in, when it differs from the block's COV_REFERENCE_FRAME.

OBJECT.description: Satellite name for the first object

CENTER_NAME.description: Origin of reference frame (EARTH, MARS, MOON, etc.)

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Name of the reference frame (TEME, EME2000, etc.)

REFERENCE_FRAME_EPOCH.description: Epoch of reference frame, if not intrinsic to the definition of the reference frame

COV_REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame for the covariance matrix

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used for the orbit state and covariance matrix. (UTC)

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

A1.description: Atomic time scale of the reference atomic-time network, offset from International Atomic Time by the fixed constant A1 - TAI = 0.0343817 s exactly. Appended last; never reorder or reuse existing values.

START_TIME.description: Start of TOTAL time span covered by ephemeris data and covariance data (ISO 8601)

USEABLE_START_TIME.description: Optional start USEABLE time span covered by ephemeris data (ISO 8601)

USEABLE_STOP_TIME.description: Optional end of USEABLE time span covered by ephemeris data (ISO 8601)

STOP_TIME.description: End of TOTAL time span covered by ephemeris data and covariance data (ISO 8601)

INTERPOLATION.description:
Recommended interpolation method for ephemeris data.
Supported methods: Hermite, Linear, Lagrange, Chebyshev.
When set to "Chebyshev", parsers should use POLYNOMIAL_POSITION_RECORDS
for high-fidelity polynomial interpolation instead of interpolating across
discrete state vectors.

INTERPOLATION_DEGREE.description: Recommended interpolation degree for ephemeris data

STEP_SIZE.description:
Time interval between ephemeris states in seconds.
If > 0: Use compact EPHEMERIS_DATA array (times are implicit).
If 0 or omitted: Use EPHEMERIS_DATA_LINES with explicit epochs.

STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.description:
Number of components per state vector in EPHEMERIS_DATA array.
6 = position + velocity (X, Y, Z, X_DOT, Y_DOT, Z_DOT)
9 = position + velocity + acceleration (adds X_DDOT, Y_DDOT, Z_DDOT)
Only used when STEP_SIZE > 0. Default is 6.

EPHEMERIS_DATA.description:
Compact ephemeris data as row-major array of doubles.
Only used when STEP_SIZE > 0.
Layout: [x0,y0,z0,xdot0,ydot0,zdot0, x1,y1,z1,xdot1,ydot1,zdot1, ...]
Units: position in km, velocity in km/s, acceleration in km/s²
Length must be divisible by STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.
Number of states = length(EPHEMERIS_DATA) / STATE_VECTOR_SIZE

EPHEMERIS_DATA_LINES.description:
Array of ephemeris data lines with explicit epochs.
Only used when STEP_SIZE == 0 or omitted (non-uniform time steps).
Each line contains its own EPOCH timestamp.

POLYNOMIAL_POSITION_RECORDS.description:
Optional polynomial position records for high-fidelity interpolation.
Used when INTERPOLATION is "Chebyshev". Each record covers a time segment with
polynomial coefficients for continuous position (and optionally velocity) evaluation.
See PPE schema for record structure and evaluation procedure.

OBJECT_NAIF_ID.description: NAIF integer code of the ephemeris target (SPK segment target).

CENTER_NAIF_ID.description:
NAIF integer code of the ephemeris centre, matching CENTER_NAME
(SPK segment centre).

CLASSIFICATION.description:
OEM Header
Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

COMMENT.description: COMMENT lines of the OEM header (CCSDS 502.0-B-3), joined by a line feed.

MESSAGE_ID.description:
MESSAGE_ID of the OEM header (CCSDS 502.0-B-3): an identifier the originator
makes unique for this message.

SIGMA_U.description: Position uncertainty along U, radial, in the UVW frame of this state (km, 1-sigma)

SIGMA_V.description: Position uncertainty along V, in-track, in the UVW frame of this state (km, 1-sigma)

SIGMA_W.description: Position uncertainty along W, cross-track, in the UVW frame of this state (km, 1-sigma)

MNV.description:
Spacecraft Maneuver

U, V and W are the UVW axes of an orbit state: U radial, along the position
vector away from the central body; W cross-track, along the orbit normal
(the direction of r x v); V in-track, W x U, completing the right-handed
frame. DELTA_VEL_U/V/W and DELTA_POS_U/V/W are in the UVW frame of the
pre-maneuver state at EVENT_START_TIME.

EVENT_ID.description:
Maneuver event identifier. Records of one event share it: a merged event
and the source records it combines.

MNVR_ACCELS.description:
Acceleration values (km/s^2): U, V and W per point, in the UVW frame of
the state at that point's MNVR_ACCEL_TIMES entry

SOURCED_DATA.description:
Sourced data references: identifiers of the records this one was
determined from (CIDv1 for records of this network), such as the source
records a merged event combines

PROVENANCE.description: Where the maneuver's data comes from and the terms it travels under.

PNM.description:
Publish Notification Message.

PNM is the compact network announcement for a published record, manifest, or
dataset update. For dataset updates, FILE_ID is the complete canonical
identity for the published update and CID usually points to a small DPM
manifest or digest. The DPM carries the full verification contract:
provider identity, retrieval protocol, canonical query, result hash, Merkle
roots, completeness-capable indexes, file_id partition key, and signature.
Large or paid dataset updates do not need to be published as globally
discoverable IPFS files; a PNM may instead advertise a provider-mediated SDN
query protocol. In that mode the PNM is only the announcement. The DPM is
the signed commitment, and each provider response carries records plus
Merkle proof material that the subscriber verifies against the DPM roots and
the announced FILE_ID before import.

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description:
Multiformat Address
As specified by the multiaddr specification.
A universal address format for representing multiple network protocols. Examples include:
- /ip4/192.168.1.1/tcp/80 for an IPv4 address with TCP protocol
- /ip6zone/x/ip6/::1 for an IPv6 address with a zone
- /dns4/example.com for a domain name resolvable only to IPv4 addresses
- /ipfs/bafybeiccfclkdtucu6y4yc5cpr6y3yuinr67svmii46v5cfcrkp47ihehy/README.txt -IPFS address w/CID and path to `README.txt`.

PUBLISH_TIMESTAMP.description: Publish Time OF THE Publish Notification Message

CID.description:
Concatenated Content Identifier (CID)
This field is a unique ID for distributed systems (CID).
The CID provides a unique identifier within distributed systems, as
detailed in the multiformats CID specification.
For dataset-update PNMs this SHOULD identify a compact DPM manifest,
manifest digest, or other small verification object, not necessarily the
full dataset bytes.

FILE_NAME.description:
File ID
This field is the Name

FILE_ID.description:
File ID
Canonical publication/update partition identity. For dataset-update PNMs,
this MUST match DPM.FILE_ID and is the stable key used everywhere an SDN
component refers to the update: PNMs, DPMs, assets, entitlements, provider
query requests, subscriber caches, replay, audit, and completeness
verification. Provider-mediated query requests and responses MUST bind
their Merkle leaves and proof paths to this FILE_ID, and subscribers MUST
reject responses whose DPM, records, or proofs bind to a different FILE_ID.
Example: provider-slug:gp:OMM.fbs:2026-05-06T03:00:00Z.

SIGNATURE.description:
Digital Signature of the CID
This is the digital signature of the CID, signed using the specified cryptographic method.

TIMESTAMP_SIGNATURE.description:
Timestamp Signature
Digital signature of the publish timestamp, using the specified cryptographic method for timestamp verification.

SIGNATURE_TYPE.description:
Type of Cryptographic Signature Used
Specifies the type of cryptographic signature used for the SIGNATURE field, indicating the specific blockchain technology, such as Ethereum or BTC.

TIMESTAMP_SIGNATURE_TYPE.description:
Type of Cryptographic Signature Used for Timestamp
Specifies the type of cryptographic signature used for the TIMESTAMP_SIGNATURE field, indicating the specific blockchain technology, such as Ethereum or BTC.

CryptoKey.description:
Represents cryptographic key information.

The publication paradigm is "literal public keys, not derivation
material": a published EPM carries the PUBLIC_KEY bytes that verify
the record's SIGNATURE (signing) or encrypt to the entity (encryption),
and NOTHING about how those keys were derived. XPUB, KEY_PATH and
KEY_ADDRESS are PRIVATE / operational — they belong to the wallet that
produced the keys, never to the record a peer resolves.

Requiredness is PROFILE-ENFORCED, never a flatc `(required)` attribute:
a `(required)` on PUBLIC_KEY would make the flatbuffers Verifier reject
every pre-flip secp256k1 record that legitimately omitted it (the
2026-07-27 dual-curve regime allowed xpub-derivation for secp at
non-hardened paths). A published record is self-describing instead —
PUBLIC_KEY present, XPUB/KEY_PATH/KEY_ADDRESS absent — and a conformance
checker asserts that profile (see scripts/check-epm-published-profile.mjs).

Rotation is by republish: a new signing or encryption key means a new
PUBLIC_KEY, a re-signed SIGNATURE, and a re-published EPM at the same
peer-addressed location. The PeerID (multihash of the libp2p identity
pubkey) is the stable anchor across rotations.

PUBLIC_KEY.description:
Public part of the cryptographic key, in hexadecimal format. AUTHORITATIVE
in a published record: this is the verifying/encrypting key, and no other
field yields it. Required-in-practice (profile-enforced, not flatc
`(required)`) so that pre-flip secp256k1 records without it still decode.

XPUB.description:
Extended public key, as specified by BIP-32 (hierarchical deterministic
wallets), "Extended keys". PRIVATE / operational: present only in the
wallet that derived the keys, ABSENT from published records. A verifier
never derives a child key from XPUB — the PUBLIC_KEY is the verification
material.

PRIVATE_KEY.description: Private part of the cryptographic key in hexidecimal format, should be kept secret

XPRIV.description: Extended private key, as specified by BIP-32 (hierarchical deterministic wallets), "Extended keys".

KEY_ADDRESS.description:
Address generated from the cryptographic key. PRIVATE / operational in a
published EPM: a chain address is bound through a ChainProof attestation,
not carried as a standalone KEY_ADDRESS on the CryptoKey. ABSENT from
published records.

ADDRESS_TYPE.description:
Type of the address generated from the cryptographic key. An address
format tag only — NOT a curve or algorithm designator; the algorithm
lives in ALGORITHM

KEY_TYPE.description: Type of the cryptographic key (signing or encryption)

KEY_PATH.description:
BIP-32 / SLIP-10 derivation path of this key from the entity root
(e.g., "m/44'/0'/0'/0/0" secp256k1 non-hardened, "m/44'/0'/0'/0'/0'"
ed25519 hardened). PRIVATE / operational: how the key was derived belongs
to the wallet, not to a published record. ABSENT from published records.

ALGORITHM.description:
Key algorithm/curve (e.g., "ed25519", "secp256k1"). ABSENT means
ed25519: every record published before this field existed verifies
unchanged under that default. The verifier dispatches on ALGORITHM (not
on ADDRESS_TYPE, which is an address-format tag only).

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format produced by this key (e.g., "raw-ed25519",
"der"). ABSENT means the canonical encoding of ALGORITHM: raw-ed25519
for ed25519 (64 bytes over the content itself); der for secp256k1, a
strict DER ECDSA signature over ONE SHA-256 of the canonical signing
content (CANONICAL_SERIALIZATION.md section 4). The signer passes the
content to a hashing signer, or its single SHA-256 to a digest signer,
never a digest to a hashing signer: ECDSA over SHA-256(SHA-256(content))
does not verify. "compact" (65-byte header||r||s) is a ChainProof
encoding only, never the EPM signature's

REGION.description: Region of the address (e.g., state or province)

LOCALITY.description: Locality of the address (e.g., city or town)

ChainProof.description: Proves a blockchain key derives from the same HD wallet as the signing key

SIGNATURE.description:
Signature over the attestation payload (hex-encoded), in the chain's
own signed-message form (see ALGORITHM)

SIGNED_PAYLOAD.description: The canonical payload that was signed (hex-encoded)

ALGORITHM.description:
Signature algorithm, which fixes the one hash the signature is over:
"secp256k1-compact-bitcoin": the Bitcoin signed-message hash
SHA-256(SHA-256("\x18Bitcoin Signed Message:\n" || CompactSize(len)
|| SIGNED_PAYLOAD)), as Bitcoin Core's signmessage signs it (the
double SHA-256 is the protocol's own, applied once);
"secp256k1-compact-ethereum": the EIP-191 personal_sign hash
Keccak-256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" || decimal(len) ||
SIGNED_PAYLOAD), low-S;
"ed25519": raw Ed25519 over SIGNED_PAYLOAD itself.
Both secp256k1 forms are the 65-byte compact recoverable signature
header||r||s (header 27 + recovery id, +4 for a compressed key; signers
emit 31 + recovery id). A verifier hashes SIGNED_PAYLOAD with the chain's
protocol, recovers the key and compares it with PUBLIC_KEY (33-byte
compressed). Nothing hashes the payload before the protocol hash.

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format: "compact" for the secp256k1 algorithms
(65-byte header||r||s), "raw-ed25519" for ed25519

DomainProof.description:
Proves control of one or more DNS domains by the same HD wallet as the
signing key — the EPM-record mirror of the DNS TXT wire form (which is
deliberately NON-SDS: a base64 FlatBuffer would not fit a 255-byte TXT
record). The canonical statement is a fixed layout of LF-terminated lines,
versioned by its first line, that names every domain of DOMAINS, and it
verifies by BYTE-REPLAY of the verbatim SIGNED_PAYLOAD (ChainProof
precedent) — never by JCS.

DNS_DOMAIN.description:
Retired slot. Buffers written by SDS 1.265.0 (DNS_DOMAIN) and by 1.264.0
and earlier (DOMAIN) carry one domain string here. The slot is deprecated
in place — never retyped, renamed or reused — so those buffers still
decode; generated code has no accessor for it. Read DOMAINS.

KEY_PATH.description:
BIP-32 / SLIP-10 derivation path of the proving key. The signer is the
Ed25519 EPM/publication key at m/44'/0'/0'/0'/0'

SIGNED_PAYLOAD.description: The canonical payload that was signed, verbatim (hex-encoded)

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format. ABSENT means the canonical encoding of
ALGORITHM (raw-ed25519 for ed25519)

DOMAINS.description:
The fully-qualified domain names the proof binds, one or more, each
lowercase ASCII (internationalized names in punycode), e.g.
["node.example.org", "node.example.com"]. An empty vector is invalid.
SIGNED_PAYLOAD covers every name, in this order.

LEGAL_NAME.description: Common name of the entity (person or organization)

FAMILY_NAME.description: Family name or surname of the person

GIVEN_NAME.description: Given name or first name of the person

ADDITIONAL_NAME.description: Additional name or middle name of the person

HONORIFIC_PREFIX.description: Honorific prefix preceding the person's name (e.g., Mr., Dr.)

HONORIFIC_SUFFIX.description: Honorific suffix following the person's name (e.g., Jr., Sr.)

KEYS.description: Cryptographic keys associated with the entity

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description: Multiformat addresses associated with the entity

SIGNATURE.description:
Signature over canonical EPM content (hex), produced by the entity's
signing key under the algorithm declared in SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM
(absent declaration = Ed25519)

SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the EPM was signed

CHAIN_PROOFS.description: Chain binding proofs linking blockchain keys to the same HD wallet

ENTITY_TYPE.description: Type of entity represented by this profile

SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.description:
Signature algorithm that produced SIGNATURE (e.g., "ed25519",
"secp256k1"). ABSENT means ed25519 — this single default is what keeps
every EPM signed before this field existed verifying unchanged, so the
field MUST NOT be made required. The signing key is the first CryptoKey
in KEYS with KEY_TYPE Signing whose ALGORITHM matches this declaration
(an absent CryptoKey.ALGORITHM likewise means ed25519)

DOMAIN_PROOFS.description:
DNS domain binding proofs linking domains to the same HD wallet —
symmetric with CHAIN_PROOFS

PHOTO.description:
Photo or logo of the entity (the vCard PHOTO property), as an RFC 2397
data URI carrying a JPEG or PNG image, e.g.
"data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ…". Every peer that resolves the entity
fetches the record, so a producer keeps the image small (a few tens of
kilobytes at most). Signed like every other content field: it
participates in the canonical preimage (CANONICAL_SERIALIZATION.md)

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference Frame in which the object position is defined

AREA_SRP.description: Area of the object solar radiation pressure

X.description: X-coordinate of the object's position in RTN coordinates

Y.description: Y-coordinate of the object's position in RTN

Z.description: Z-coordinate of the object's position in RTN

X_DOT.description: X-coordinate of the object's position in RTN coordinates

Y_DOT.description: Y-coordinate of the object's position in RTN

Z_DOT.description: Z-coordinate of the object's position in RTN

COVARIANCE.description:
Covariance matrix as flat array (9x9 lower triangular = 45 elements).
Order: [CR_R, CT_R, CT_T, CN_R, CN_T, CN_N, CRDOT_R, CRDOT_T, CRDOT_N, CRDOT_RDOT,
CTDOT_R, CTDOT_T, CTDOT_N, CTDOT_RDOT, CTDOT_TDOT,
CNDOT_R, CNDOT_T, CNDOT_N, CNDOT_RDOT, CNDOT_TDOT, CNDOT_NDOT,
CDRG_R, CDRG_T, CDRG_N, CDRG_RDOT, CDRG_TDOT, CDRG_NDOT, CDRG_DRG,
CSRP_R, CSRP_T, CSRP_N, CSRP_RDOT, CSRP_TDOT, CSRP_NDOT, CSRP_DRG, CSRP_SRP,
CTHR_R, CTHR_T, CTHR_N, CTHR_RDOT, CTHR_TDOT, CTHR_NDOT, CTHR_DRG, CTHR_SRP, CTHR_THR]

OBJECT_DESIGNATOR.description:
OBJECT_DESIGNATOR (CCSDS 508.0-B-1): the object's identifier in CATALOG_NAME,
as written. A numeric designator is also OBJECT.NORAD_CAT_ID.

CATALOG_NAME.description: CATALOG_NAME (CCSDS 508.0-B-1): the satellite catalog OBJECT_DESIGNATOR is in.

MANEUVERABLE.description:
MANEUVERABLE (CCSDS 508.0-B-1): YES, NO or N/A. OBJECT.MANEUVERABLE holds the
same fact as a flag, true for YES.

CD_AREA_OVER_MASS.description: CD_AREA_OVER_MASS (CCSDS 508.0-B-1): drag area over mass, m**2/kg.

CDM.description:
Conjunction Data Message

Units of the record: lengths in km (MISS_DISTANCE, RELATIVE_POSITION_*,
SCREEN_VOLUME_*, X, Y, Z), speeds in km/s, and the 6x6 position/velocity part
of each object's COVARIANCE (the first 21 cells) in km**2, km**2/s and
km**2/s**2. The message text states metres: CCSDS 508.0-B-1 gives
MISS_DISTANCE = 715 [m], which this record holds as 0.715. The cells of
COVARIANCE beyond the first 21 (the drag, solar radiation pressure and thrust
terms) are held as the message states them.

CCSDS_CDM_VERS.description: The version of the CCSDS CDM standard used

CREATION_DATE.description: The date the CDM message was created

ORIGINATOR.description: The originator of the CDM message

MESSAGE_FOR.description: The intended recipient of the CDM message

MESSAGE_ID.description: A unique identifier for the CDM message

MISS_DISTANCE.description: The miss distance between the two objects

RELATIVE_SPEED.description: The relative speed between the two objects

START_SCREEN_PERIOD.description: The start time of the screening period

STOP_SCREEN_PERIOD.description: The end time of the screening period

SCREEN_VOLUME_FRAME.description: The reference frame for the screening volume

SCREEN_VOLUME_SHAPE.description: The shape of the screening volume

SCREEN_VOLUME_X.description: The X dimension of the screening volume

SCREEN_VOLUME_Y.description: The Y dimension of the screening volume

SCREEN_VOLUME_Z.description: The Z dimension of the screening volume

SCREEN_ENTRY_TIME.description: The time the objects entered the screening volume

SCREEN_EXIT_TIME.description: The time the objects exited the screening volume

COLLISION_PROBABILITY.description: The probability of collision between the two objects

COLLISION_PROBABILITY_METHOD.description: The method used to calculate the collision probability

OBJECT1.description: The first object in the CDM message

OBJECT2.description: The second object in the CDM message

OBJECT1_DATASOURCE.description: Data Source for the positional information for Object 1

OBJECT2_DATASOURCE.description: Data Source for the positional information for Object 2

COMMENT.description:
COMMENT lines of the message header and of its relative metadata and data
(CCSDS 508.0-B-1), in message order, joined by a line feed.

mplElements.description:
Classical (osculating) orbital elements of one orbit. In a request the
first fields describe the orbit; in an answer the derived fields are
filled too.

SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_KM.description: Semi-major axis, km; negative for a hyperbola.

RAAN_DEG.description: Right ascension of the ascending node, deg.

TRUE_ANOMALY_DEG.description:
True anomaly, deg; NaN = not stated (MEAN_ANOMALY_DEG places the
object instead).

MEAN_ANOMALY_DEG.description: Mean anomaly, deg; NaN = not stated.

ECCENTRIC_ANOMALY_DEG.description: Eccentric anomaly, deg; NaN = not stated.

MU_KM3_S2.description:
Gravitational parameter of the central body, km^3/s^2; 0 = the plan's
MU_KM3_S2.

ANGULAR_MOMENTUM_KM2_S.description: Specific angular momentum, km^2/s; 0 = derived from the elements.

PERIOD_S.description: Orbital period, s; 0 = not computed or not closed.

PERIAPSIS_RADIUS_KM.description: Periapsis radius from the body centre, km; 0 = not computed.

APOAPSIS_RADIUS_KM.description: Apoapsis radius from the body centre, km; 0 = not computed or none.

ASCENDING_NODE_TRUE_ANOMALY_DEG.description: True anomaly of the ascending node, deg; NaN = not computed.

MEAN_ARGUMENT_OF_LATITUDE_DEG.description:
Mean argument of latitude (argument of periapsis + mean anomaly), deg;
NaN = not computed.

mplOrbit.description:
One orbit, given by EXACTLY ONE of ELEMENTS or STATE. A request that
carries both, or neither, is invalid: the form is always stated, never
inferred.

OBJECT_ID.description:
Identifier of the object on this orbit (catalog number, international
designator or name); empty = not stated.

STATE.description:
Inertial state in the plan's REFERENCE_FRAME (km, km/s). EPOCH empty =
the plan's start (PLAN_EPOCH_MS, or offset 0).

mplBurn.description: One impulsive (or short finite) burn of a plan.

NAME.description: Label of the burn within the plan, e.g. "departure", "circularize".

EPOCH_MS.description:
Unix milliseconds of the burn (its start for a finite burn); 0 = not
anchored to an absolute time (use OFFSET_S).

OFFSET_S.description: Seconds from the plan's start (PLAN_EPOCH_MS) to the burn.

TRUE_ANOMALY_DEG.description:
True anomaly on the orbit being left at which to burn, deg; NaN = not
stated.

Inertial.description: The inertial frame of the plan (REFERENCE_FRAME); components x, y, z.

RIC.description: Radial, in-track, cross-track: R = r/|r|, C = (r x v)/|r x v|, I = C x R; components ordered R, I, C. The same triad as $MNV's U, V, W and $RFM's ORBITAL_RADIAL_TRANSVERSE_NORMAL.

VNC.description: Velocity, normal, co-normal: V = v/|v|, N = (r x v)/|r x v|, C = V x N; components ordered V, N, C. Differs from RIC away from the apsides.

DELTA_V.description:
Delta-v vector, km/s, 3 values in AXES order. Components are signed (a
retrograde in-track burn has a negative I component).

REFERENCE_ORBIT.description:
The orbit the burn's axes are built from (the chaser's for an absolute
burn, the reference orbit at the burn for a relative-motion leg); empty
= the plan's initial orbit.

ARC_INDEX.description: Index into ARCS of the arc this burn starts; -1 = none (the final burn).

MANEUVER_ID.description:
Identifier of the $MNV this burn became once committed; empty until
then.

mplTrajectory.description:
States sampled along an arc or a whole plan, column-major and parallel:
OFFSETS_S has one entry per sample and STATES has STATE_SIZE entries per
sample.

AXES.description:
Axes and origin of STATES: Inertial = the plan's REFERENCE_FRAME about
the central body; RIC or VNC = relative to the reference orbit (the
target), centred on it.

Inertial.description: The inertial frame of the plan (REFERENCE_FRAME); components x, y, z.

RIC.description: Radial, in-track, cross-track: R = r/|r|, C = (r x v)/|r x v|, I = C x R; components ordered R, I, C. The same triad as $MNV's U, V, W and $RFM's ORBITAL_RADIAL_TRANSVERSE_NORMAL.

VNC.description: Velocity, normal, co-normal: V = v/|v|, N = (r x v)/|r x v|, C = V x N; components ordered V, N, C. Differs from RIC away from the apsides.

STATE_SIZE.description:
Values per sample in STATES: 3 = position only, 6 = position and
velocity. 0 is read as 6.

OFFSETS_S.description:
Seconds from the plan's start, one per sample, signed (negative for a
track sampled backwards).

STATES.description: Positions (km) and velocities (km/s), STATE_SIZE values per sample.

mplSolver.description: Solver evidence for an arc or a plan.

CONVERGED.description: True when the solver met its tolerance.

RESIDUAL.description:
Final residual, in the solver's own measure (time of flight in s for
Lambert; position error in km for targeting).

RESIDUAL_TOLERANCE.description: The residual the solver had to meet, same unit; 0 = not stated.

mplArc.description:
One arc of a plan: a coast or transfer between burns, or a leg, phase or
segment of a relative-motion plan.

Coast.description: Coast on the initial or final orbit.

Leg.description: One leg of a relative waypoint mission.

START_OFFSET_S.description: Seconds from the plan's start to the arc's start.

DURATION_S.description: Duration of the arc, s (time of flight for a transfer).

REVOLUTIONS.description:
Revolutions completed on the arc (Lambert revolution count, phasing
revolutions); 0 = less than one.

Unspecified.description: No branch: zero revolutions (the solution is unique) or not stated.

Low.description: The first time-of-flight crossing of the revolution count.

High.description: The second time-of-flight crossing of the revolution count.

SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_KM.description:
Semi-major axis of the arc's conic, km; 0 = not representable
(parabola) or not computed.

PERIAPSIS_RADIUS_KM.description:
Periapsis radius from the body centre, km. Reported, never a refusal: an
arc may pass below the body surface, and the consumer screens.

APOAPSIS_RADIUS_KM.description: Apoapsis radius, km; 0 = none (parabolic or hyperbolic).

PERIOD_S.description: Period of the arc's orbit, s; 0 = not closed or not computed.

START_STATE.description:
State at the arc's start (position and velocity just after the burn
that starts it). Inertial (km, km/s) unless STATE_AXES says relative.

END_STATE.description: State at the arc's end (just before the burn that ends it).

Inertial.description: The inertial frame of the plan (REFERENCE_FRAME); components x, y, z.

RIC.description: Radial, in-track, cross-track: R = r/|r|, C = (r x v)/|r x v|, I = C x R; components ordered R, I, C. The same triad as $MNV's U, V, W and $RFM's ORBITAL_RADIAL_TRANSVERSE_NORMAL.

VNC.description: Velocity, normal, co-normal: V = v/|v|, N = (r x v)/|r x v|, C = V x N; components ordered V, N, C. Differs from RIC away from the apsides.

DELTA_V_KM_S.description:
Delta-v of the burns that start and end this arc, km/s; 0 = not
computed.

LAMBERT_Z.description: Universal variable z of a Lambert solution (dimensionless); 0 elsewhere.

TRAJECTORY.description: Sampled states along the arc; empty = not sampled.

mplOption.description:
An option the planner weighed: another revolution count or branch of a
Lambert problem, or the other phasing direction. Lets a consumer show the
road not taken beside the chosen plan.

SELECTED.description: True for the option the plan carries.

Unspecified.description: No branch: zero revolutions (the solution is unique) or not stated.

Low.description: The first time-of-flight crossing of the revolution count.

High.description: The second time-of-flight crossing of the revolution count.

Shortest.description: Whichever of catching up or falling behind is the smaller angle.

CatchUp.description: The chaser gains phase (relative phase angle in (0, 360] deg).

FallBehind.description: The chaser loses phase (relative phase angle in [-360, 0) deg).

PHASE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Phase angle this option closes, deg (signed).

BURN_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Magnitude of each burn, km/s, in burn order.

SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_KM.description: Semi-major axis of the option's transfer or phasing orbit, km.

CLAMPED_TO_FLOOR.description: True when the option's orbit was clamped to the body's floor.

WITHIN_BUDGET.description: True when the option met the delta-v budget.

mplTransferRequest.description:
Classical transfer and plane change between circular orbits (Hohmann,
BiElliptic, PlaneChange, CombinedTransfer).

INITIAL_RADIUS_KM.description:
Radius of the initial circular orbit, km (also the orbit radius of a
PlaneChange).

FINAL_RADIUS_KM.description: Radius of the final circular orbit, km.

INTERMEDIATE_RADIUS_KM.description: Apoapsis radius of the intermediate orbit of a BiElliptic transfer, km.

SPEED_KM_S.description: Orbital speed at the burn of a PlaneChange, km/s.

mplLambertRequest.description:
Lambert problem (Lambert, LambertMinimumDeltaV). DEPARTURE and ARRIVAL
give the two positions; their velocities, when given, are the velocities
of the orbits being left and joined, and make the result's burns real
delta-v (LambertMinimumDeltaV requires them, since ranking needs a cost).

DEPARTURE.description: Departure position (and the departing orbit's velocity), inertial.

ARRIVAL.description: Arrival position (and the arrival orbit's velocity), inertial.

ENDPOINT_VELOCITIES.description:
True when DEPARTURE and ARRIVAL carry orbit velocities; false = position
only (the result then gives the transfer velocities, not delta-v).

PROGRADE.description: True for a prograde (short-way in the direction of motion) transfer.

REVOLUTIONS.description:
Revolution count of a Lambert problem; the largest count ranked by
LambertMinimumDeltaV.

BRANCH.description:
Lambert: the arc to return when REVOLUTIONS >= 1 (Unspecified = Low).
LambertMinimumDeltaV: narrows the ranking to one branch (Unspecified =
rank both).

Unspecified.description: No branch: zero revolutions (the solution is unique) or not stated.

Low.description: The first time-of-flight crossing of the revolution count.

High.description: The second time-of-flight crossing of the revolution count.

ORBIT_RADIUS_KM.description: Phasing: radius of the chaser's circular orbit, km.

PHASE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Phasing: phase angle to close, deg; positive when the target leads.

REVOLUTIONS.description: Revolutions on the phasing orbit; read only when HAS_REVOLUTIONS.

HAS_REVOLUTIONS.description:
True when REVOLUTIONS is stated (0 is then a real request for zero
revolutions, which a planner may refuse); false = recommend the
smallest count that neither clamps to the floor nor exceeds the budget
(Phasing: the planner's default count).

MAX_REVOLUTIONS.description:
Largest revolution count a recommendation may use; 0 = the planner's
default (a planner searches at least one revolution).

Shortest.description: Whichever of catching up or falling behind is the smaller angle.

CatchUp.description: The chaser gains phase (relative phase angle in (0, 360] deg).

FallBehind.description: The chaser loses phase (relative phase angle in [-360, 0) deg).

DELTA_V_BUDGET_KM_S.description:
Delta-v budget, km/s; 0 = DELTA_V_BUDGET_FRACTION of the chaser's
circular speed.

DELTA_V_BUDGET_FRACTION.description:
Budget as a fraction of the chaser's circular speed; 0 = the planner's
default (0.01).

COPLANAR_TOLERANCE_DEG.description:
Largest angle between the two orbit normals still called coplanar, deg;
read only when HAS_COPLANAR_TOLERANCE (false = the planner's default).

ECCENTRICITY_TOLERANCE.description:
Largest eccentricity still called near-circular; read only when
HAS_ECCENTRICITY_TOLERANCE (false = the planner's default).

CO_ORBITAL_TOLERANCE.description:
Largest semi-major-axis difference still called co-orbital, in the unit
CO_ORBITAL_TOLERANCE_BASIS states (km, or a fraction of the chaser's
semi-major axis); read only when HAS_CO_ORBITAL_TOLERANCE (false = the
planner's default).

RelativeToChaserSemiMajorAxis.description: A fraction of the chaser's semi-major axis (dimensionless).

mplDifferentialDrag.description: A differential-drag model for relative motion.

MODEL.description: Which drag model; J2DragEccentric or J2DragArbitrary.

J2DragEccentric.description: J2 with differential drag, eccentric-orbit drag model.

J2DragArbitrary.description: J2 with differential drag, arbitrary differential-drag model.

DA_DOT_PER_S.description:
Differential drag rates of the dimensionless relative orbital
elements, 1/s: of the relative semi-major axis da (multiply by the
reference semi-major axis for a length rate), and of the relative
eccentricity-vector components dex and dey. DA_DOT_PER_S alone for
J2DragEccentric; all three for J2DragArbitrary.

POSITION_KM.description: Position relative to the reference orbit, RIC, km, 3 values.

VELOCITY_KM_S.description: Velocity to arrive with, RIC, km/s, 3 values; empty = free.

TIME_OF_FLIGHT_S.description: Time of flight of the leg to this waypoint, s; 0 = the planner chooses.

mplRelativeRequest.description:
Relative-motion planning about a reference orbit
(RelativeStateTransition, RelativeWaypoints, CollisionAvoidance,
ApproachCorridor).

RELATIVE_STATE.description: Chaser state relative to the reference, RIC, km and km/s.

DYNAMICS.description:
Dynamics of propagation and targeting: RelativeStateTransition
propagates INITIAL_ROE with these (J2 on or off; the drag model is
DRAG); the targeting problems plan with them.

J2DragEccentric.description: J2 with differential drag, eccentric-orbit drag model.

J2DragArbitrary.description: J2 with differential drag, arbitrary differential-drag model.

STM_DYNAMICS.description:
RelativeStateTransition: dynamics of the state transition matrix
returned, chosen independently of DYNAMICS (e.g. a Keplerian matrix
beside a J2 propagation). J2DragEccentric and J2DragArbitrary also
return the drag columns.

J2DragEccentric.description: J2 with differential drag, eccentric-orbit drag model.

J2DragArbitrary.description: J2 with differential drag, arbitrary differential-drag model.

INITIAL_ROE.description:
RelativeStateTransition: quasi-nonsingular relative orbital elements to
propagate (da, dlambda, dex, dey, dix, diy), dimensionless; empty = the
transition matrix only.

TARGET_VELOCITY_KM_S.description:
Targeting: velocity to arrive with at every waypoint without its own,
RIC, km/s, 3 values; empty = free.

LEG_TIME_LOWER_ORBITS.description:
Shortest and longest leg time the planner may choose, in reference
orbits; 0 = default.

SAMPLES_PER_LEG.description: States sampled per leg in the answer's trajectory; 0 = default.

TIME_TO_CLOSEST_APPROACH_S.description: CollisionAvoidance: time from now to closest approach, s.

MAX_DELTA_V_KM_S.description:
CollisionAvoidance: delta-v available, km/s; read only when
HAS_MAX_DELTA_V. When stated, 0 = unlimited.

HAS_MAX_DELTA_V.description:
True when MAX_DELTA_V_KM_S is stated; false = the planner's default
limit.

PREFER_RADIAL.description: CollisionAvoidance: prefer radial burns (they preserve the period).

CONJUNCTION.description:
CollisionAvoidance: the conjunction being avoided, when the request
comes from a conjunction data message.

APPROACH_TARGET_KM.description: ApproachCorridor: point to reach, RIC, km, 3 values.

APPROACH_SPEED_KM_S.description: ApproachCorridor: speed at the target point, km/s.

CORRIDOR_HALF_WIDTH_KM.description: ApproachCorridor: half-width of the safety corridor, km.

mplRendezvousRequest.description:
Closed-loop rendezvous in the target's RIC axes: a free-drift leg to a
brake point, a fifth-order braking profile to a hold point, and a hold,
tracked by a feedback controller and propagated on a truth model.

INITIAL_POSITION_KM.description: Chaser's starting position, RIC, km, 3 values.

INITIAL_VELOCITY_KM_S.description:
Chaser's starting velocity, RIC, km/s, 3 values; empty = solve it so
the drift leg reaches BRAKE_POINT_KM after DRIFT_DURATION_S.

HOLD_POINT_KM.description: Hold point reached with zero relative velocity, RIC, km, 3 values.

BANDWIDTH_RAD_S.description: Closed-loop natural frequency, rad/s; 0 = ten times the mean motion.

DAMPING_RATIO.description:
Closed-loop damping ratio; read only when HAS_DAMPING_RATIO (false = 1,
critically damped).

KP_PER_S2.description:
Proportional gain, 1/s^2; read only when HAS_KP (false = from the
bandwidth).

KD_PER_S.description:
Derivative gain, 1/s; read only when HAS_KD (false = from the damping
ratio).

FEEDFORWARD.description: Apply the reference acceleration as feedforward.

COMPENSATE_CORIOLIS.description: Cancel the Coriolis coupling of the relative dynamics.

TIME_STEP_S.description: Integration step and control period, s; 0 = 1 s.

OUTPUT_EVERY.description:
Log every Nth step to the answer's samples (the last step always); 0 =
default.

INCLUDE_J2.description: Include J2 in the truth gravity.

mplGeometryRequest.description:
Orbit-geometry questions (OrbitGeometry, AnomalyConversion,
TimeOfFlight, OrbitSampling, DeltaVTransform).

ORBIT.description: The orbit asked about (all but AnomalyConversion).

AT_TRUE_ANOMALY_DEG.description:
OrbitGeometry: evaluate at this true anomaly, deg; NaN = at the orbit's
own epoch (or after ELAPSED_S). Not together with HAS_ELAPSED.

ELAPSED_S.description:
OrbitGeometry: coast this long from the orbit's epoch first, s (signed);
read only when HAS_ELAPSED.

HAS_ELAPSED.description:
True when ELAPSED_S is stated (0 is then a real zero-length coast);
false = no coast.

BURN.description:
OrbitGeometry: a burn to apply at the evaluated point;
DeltaVTransform: the delta-v to rotate (its AXES is the source axes).

TO_AXES.description: DeltaVTransform: axes to rotate the delta-v into.

Inertial.description: The inertial frame of the plan (REFERENCE_FRAME); components x, y, z.

RIC.description: Radial, in-track, cross-track: R = r/|r|, C = (r x v)/|r x v|, I = C x R; components ordered R, I, C. The same triad as $MNV's U, V, W and $RFM's ORBITAL_RADIAL_TRANSVERSE_NORMAL.

VNC.description: Velocity, normal, co-normal: V = v/|v|, N = (r x v)/|r x v|, C = V x N; components ordered V, N, C. Differs from RIC away from the apsides.

ANOMALY_DEG.description: AnomalyConversion: the anomaly to convert, deg.

FROM_TRUE_ANOMALY_DEG.description: TimeOfFlight and OrbitSampling: start true anomaly, deg.

SWEEP_DEG.description:
OrbitSampling: signed sweep from FROM_TRUE_ANOMALY_DEG, deg, at most one
revolution; read only when HAS_SWEEP.

HAS_SWEEP.description: True when SWEEP_DEG is stated; false = one full revolution forward.

mplRequest.description:
The question: which problem and its inputs. Only the sub-table matching
PROBLEM is read.

MU_KM3_S2.description:
Gravitational parameter of the central body, km^3/s^2; 0 = Earth
(398600.4418).

mplPhasingSolution.description: Phasing detail: the phase geometry and the floor guard.

PHASE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Phase angle the plan closes, deg (signed).

ACHIEVED_PHASE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Phase angle the flown (possibly clamped) phasing orbit delivers, deg.

REQUESTED_SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_KM.description: Semi-major axis and period the unclamped plan would have needed.

FLOOR_RADIUS_KM.description:
Lowest radius the phasing orbit's far apse may reach, km (body radius
plus margin).

CLAMPED_TO_FLOOR.description: True when the phasing orbit was raised to the floor.

FAR_APSE_RADIUS_KM.description:
Radius of the phasing orbit's far apse (the apse opposite the burn
point: its apoapsis when raised, its periapsis when lowered), km.

PHASING_RADIUS_KM.description: The radius the plan was flown at (the chaser's semi-major axis), km.

RELATIVE_PHASE_ANGLE_DEG.description:
PhasingToTarget: relative phase angle, deg, in (-180, 180]; positive
when the target leads. The relative mean argument of latitude plus the
RAAN difference times cos(chaser inclination).

CATCH_UP_ANGLE_DEG.description:
The catch-up angle, in (0, 360], and the fall-behind angle, in
[-360, 0), deg.

Shortest.description: Whichever of catching up or falling behind is the smaller angle.

CatchUp.description: The chaser gains phase (relative phase angle in (0, 360] deg).

FallBehind.description: The chaser loses phase (relative phase angle in [-360, 0) deg).

CHASER.description:
The chaser's and target's elements as used (with their mean arguments
of latitude).

PLANE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Angle between the two orbit normals, deg.

SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS_DIFFERENCE_KM.description: Target minus chaser semi-major axis, km.

COPLANAR.description: Verdicts, each beside the tolerance that produced it (none refuses).

CO_ORBITAL_TOLERANCE_KM.description:
The co-orbital tolerance applied, as an absolute length, km, and as a
fraction of the chaser's semi-major axis (the same threshold both ways).

RECOMMENDED_REVOLUTIONS.description:
Recommended revolution count, and whether the count came from the
caller instead.

DELTA_V_BUDGET_KM_S.description: The budget applied, km/s, and whether the plan met it.

J2DragEccentric.description: J2 with differential drag, eccentric-orbit drag model.

J2DragArbitrary.description: J2 with differential drag, arbitrary differential-drag model.

J2DragEccentric.description: J2 with differential drag, eccentric-orbit drag model.

J2DragArbitrary.description: J2 with differential drag, arbitrary differential-drag model.

STATE_TRANSITION.description:
6x6 relative-orbital-element state transition matrix over DURATION_S,
row-major (36 values), dimensionless (the ROE are dimensionless).

DRAG_COLUMNS.description:
Drag sensitivity columns, row-major 6 x DRAG_COLUMN_COUNT: entry (i, k)
is the change in ROE i at DURATION_S per unit of drag rate k, the rates
being those of mplDifferentialDrag (1/s): k = 0 da-dot, 1 dex-dot, 2
dey-dot. Unit: seconds (e.g. entry (0, 0) equals
DURATION_S). J2DragEccentric gives one column (the da-dot column of the
eccentric model), J2DragArbitrary three. Empty = no drag model.

INITIAL_ROE.description: Initial and propagated relative orbital elements (6 values each).

ACHIEVED_MISS_KM.description: CollisionAvoidance: miss distance the burn achieves, km.

FEASIBLE.description:
CollisionAvoidance: true when the required miss is reachable within the
available delta-v.

CORRIDOR_DEVIATION_KM.description:
ApproachCorridor: largest lateral deviation from the corridor axis, km,
and whether it stays within the corridor.

mplRendezvousSolution.description:
Closed-loop rendezvous detail. Samples are column-major and parallel,
one entry (or three, for vectors) per sample, all in the target's RIC
axes.

MODEL_REFERENCE.description:
Model reference, e.g. "HCW drift + quintic brake + feedback-linearized
PD".

MEAN_MOTION_RAD_S.description: Mean motion of the target, rad/s.

INITIAL_VELOCITY_KM_S.description: Drift-leg initial velocity (solved or given), km/s, 3 values.

KP_PER_S2.description: Per-axis proportional (1/s^2) and derivative (1/s) gains, 3 values each.

DRIFT_END_S.description:
End of the drift and of the braking phase, and the total time, s from
the start.

SAMPLE_TIME_S.description: Sample times, s from the start.

POSITION_KM.description:
Actual and reference relative position (km) and velocity (km/s), 3
values per sample.

REFERENCE_ACCELERATION_KM_S2.description: Reference and commanded control acceleration, km/s^2, 3 per sample.

STATE.description: OrbitGeometry: the inertial state at the evaluated point (after BURN).

ELEMENTS.description:
OrbitGeometry: elements at the point (all anomalies and derived fields
filled); AnomalyConversion: the three anomalies.

RADIUS_KM.description: Distance from the body centre, km.

RIC_BASIS.description:
The RIC axes at the point, before the burn, as three inertial unit
vectors R, I, C (9 values, row by row).

VNC_BASIS.description: The VNC axes at the point, before the burn: V, N, C (9 values).

TIME_OF_FLIGHT_S.description: TimeOfFlight: forward time between the anomalies, s.

BURN.description: DeltaVTransform: the rotated delta-v (its AXES the target axes).

MPL.description: Maneuver Plan - one planning request and the plan that answers it.

ID.description: Identifier of the plan; empty = not assigned.

CREATED_AT_MS.description: Unix milliseconds the request was made (or the plan produced).

PLANNER.description: Identifier of the planning service or tool that answered.

Hohmann.description: Two-impulse coplanar transfer between circular orbits.

BiElliptic.description: Three-impulse coplanar transfer through an intermediate apoapsis.

PlaneChange.description: Inclination change at a given radius and speed.

CombinedTransfer.description: Hohmann transfer with the plane change folded into the second burn.

Lambert.description: Lambert problem: the arc between two positions in a time of flight.

LambertMinimumDeltaV.description: Lambert problem ranked over revolution counts and branches by delta-v.

Phasing.description: Phasing orbit closing a stated phase angle.

PhasingToTarget.description: Phasing from the chaser's and the target's orbits (the angle is derived).

RelativeStateTransition.description: Relative-orbital-element state transition about a reference orbit.

RelativeWaypoints.description: Two-burn legs through a list of relative waypoints.

CollisionAvoidance.description: Collision-avoidance maneuver for a required miss distance.

ApproachCorridor.description: Approach along a V-bar, R-bar or H-bar corridor.

RendezvousSimulation.description: Closed-loop rendezvous: drift, braking and hold under feedback control.

OrbitGeometry.description: State, elements and local frames at a point of an orbit.

AnomalyConversion.description: Conversion between true, mean and eccentric anomaly.

TimeOfFlight.description: Time of flight between two true anomalies.

DeltaVTransform.description: Rotation of a delta-v between the RIC and inertial axes.

PLAN_EPOCH_MS.description:
Unix milliseconds of the plan's start (offset 0); 0 = the plan is in
relative time only.

OBJECT_ID.description: The maneuvering object (chaser) and, for relative problems, the target.

REFERENCE_FRAME.description:
Inertial frame of every inertial state and Inertial-axes vector; empty =
the central body's GCRF/EME2000.

Solved.description: Solved; the result fields carry the plan.

NoSolution.description: The geometry has no solution (e.g. no Lambert arc of the requested revolution count).

Infeasible.description: A solution exists in principle but not within the stated limits (e.g. the miss distance is not reachable with the available delta-v).

SingularGeometry.description: The geometry is singular (e.g. a radial state has no orbit normal).

InvalidRequest.description: The request is malformed or a parameter is out of range.

Failed.description: The planner failed for another reason; see ERROR_MESSAGE.

ERROR_CODE.description:
Stable machine-readable reason when STATUS is not Solved, e.g.
"invalid-parameter", "no-solution"; empty otherwise.

TOTAL_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Total delta-v: the sum of burn magnitudes (the propellant budget), km/s.

TOTAL_TIME_S.description: Time from the plan's start to its end, s.

TOTAL_DELTA_MASS_KG.description: Propellant for the whole plan, kg; 0 = not computed.

SOLVER.description: Solver evidence for the plan as a whole.

OPTIONS.description: Options weighed, including the selected one.

TRAJECTORY.description: The whole plan's sampled trajectory; empty = not sampled.

PRIMARY_BODY_ID.description:
Ephemeris body codes of the larger and smaller primary (e.g. 399, 301);
0 = not stated.

MASS_RATIO.description:
Mass ratio mu = m2 / (m1 + m2), dimensionless. The larger primary sits
at x = -mu and the smaller at x = 1 - mu.

PRIMARY_MASS_KG.description: Masses of the primaries, kg; 0 = not stated.

CHARACTERISTIC_LENGTH_KM.description: Characteristic length: the distance between the primaries, km.

CHARACTERISTIC_TIME_S.description: Characteristic time: 1 / (the primaries' angular rate), s.

SYNODIC_FRAME.description:
The synodic frame as an $RFM coordinate system; empty = the convention
above, barycentre origin.

TIME.description: Non-dimensional time of the state from the trajectory's start.

tbpTrajectory.description:
A trajectory, column-major: TIMES has one entry per sample, STATES six,
STATE_TRANSITION 36 (row-major 6x6) when it was propagated.

DIMENSIONAL.description:
True when TIMES and STATES are dimensional (s, km, km/s) in FRAME;
false = non-dimensional synodic.

FRAME.description: Frame of a dimensional trajectory; empty for synodic.

EPOCH_MS.description: Unix milliseconds of time 0 of a dimensional trajectory; 0 = relative.

STATES.description: x, y, z, vx, vy, vz per sample.

STATE_TRANSITION.description:
State transition matrix from time 0, 36 values per sample; empty = not
propagated.

JACOBI.description: Jacobi constant of the trajectory (conserved in the CR3BP).

tbpLibrationPoint.description: One libration point and its linear stability.

EIGENVALUES_REAL.description:
Eigenvalues of the linearised dynamics at the point (6 each); empty =
not computed.

STABLE.description: True when every eigenvalue has a non-positive real part.

tbpPeriodicOrbit.description: A periodic orbit, or a first guess of one.

HaloNorthern.description: Halo orbit whose largest out-of-plane excursion is north (+Z).

HaloSouthern.description: Halo orbit whose largest out-of-plane excursion is south (-Z).

NearRectilinearHalo.description: Near-rectilinear halo orbit (the high-amplitude end of the halo family).

DistantRetrograde.description: Distant retrograde orbit about the smaller primary.

LongShortPeriod.description: Short- or long-period orbit about L4 or L5.

LIBRATION_POINT.description:
Libration point the orbit is about; UNSPECIFIED for orbits about a
primary (distant retrograde).

AMPLITUDE.description:
Amplitude that selects the member of the family, non-dimensional (the
out-of-plane amplitude Az for halo orbits, the in-plane amplitude Ax
for planar Lyapunov orbits).

PERILUNE_ALTITUDE_KM.description:
NRHO: perilune and apolune altitudes above the smaller primary, km; 0 =
not an NRHO request.

INITIAL_STATE.description:
The orbit's state at time 0 (on the XZ-plane crossing for symmetric
families).

PERIOD.description: Period, non-dimensional, and the same in seconds.

CORRECTED.description:
True when the orbit was differentially corrected; false = an analytic
first guess.

TOLERANCE.description:
Corrector tolerance and iteration limit used (or requested); 0 =
default.

MONODROMY.description:
Monodromy matrix (state transition over one period), row-major 6x6;
empty = not computed.

FLOQUET_REAL.description: Floquet multipliers (eigenvalues of the monodromy matrix), 6 each.

STABILITY_INDEX.description:
Stability index (|lambda_max| + 1/|lambda_max|) / 2; 1 = marginally
stable; 0 = not computed.

STABLE.description: True when the orbit is linearly stable (STABILITY_INDEX <= 1).

TRAJECTORY.description: One period of the orbit; empty = not sampled.

OUTPUT_POINTS.description: Samples in the answer, endpoints included; 0 = default.

STATE_TRANSITION.description: Also propagate the state transition matrix.

FreeReturn.description: Free-return trajectory about the smaller primary.

PoweredFlyby.description: Powered flyby of the smaller primary.

DirectInsertion.description: Direct insertion into an orbit about the smaller primary.

PARKING_ALTITUDE_KM.description: Altitude of the circular parking orbit about the larger primary, km.

TARGET_ALTITUDE_KM.description: Altitude of the final orbit about the smaller primary, km.

INCLINATION_DEG.description: Inclination of the transfer plane, deg.

TARGET_ORBIT.description: PeriodicOrbitInsertion: the orbit to insert into.

BURNS.description:
Result: departure and arrival burns (their DELTA_V in the axes they
state, km/s; offsets in seconds from departure).

TOTAL_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Result: total delta-v, km/s, and time of flight, s.

TRAJECTORY.description: Result: the transfer trajectory; empty = not sampled.

tbpStationKeeping.description: Station-keeping budget for a periodic orbit.

ORBIT.description: The orbit kept (its INITIAL_STATE, PERIOD and JACOBI at least).

PlaneCrossing.description: Correct at each crossing of the synodic XZ plane.

TargetPoint.description: Target a reference point on the periodic orbit.

EXECUTION_ERROR_FRACTION.description: Maneuver execution error, fraction of each burn, 1 sigma.

MEAN_CYCLE_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Result: mean and largest delta-v per cycle, km/s.

CYCLE_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Result: delta-v of each cycle, km/s.

BOUNDED.description: Result: true when the orbit stays bounded over the simulation.

tbpFrameConversion.description:
A state converted between the synodic and inertial frames. The inertial
frame is centred on the barycentre with its X axis along the synodic X
axis at REFERENCE_EPOCH_MS (elapsed time 0) and Z along the system's
angular momentum.

REFERENCE_EPOCH_MS.description:
Unix milliseconds when the two frames are aligned; 0 = relative time
only.
